chunks: And it is narrated from ʿĪsā ibn Aʿyan, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who gave a gift to another man while hoping for its recompense, but its owner did not recompense him until he died, and the man found his gift itself. Is it for him to take it back if he is able to do that? He said:
There is no harm in his taking it.

key_terms.بِعَيْنِهَا: in its very same form, unchanged and identifiable
key_terms.ثَوَابَهَا: its return or recompense in this context
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection
key_terms.هَدِيَّةً: a gift given from one person to another
key_terms.يُثِبْهُ: to recompense him or give him something in return
key_terms.يُرَاجِعَهَا: to reclaim it or take it back

ai.seo_question: Can a person take back a gift if it was given expecting recompense and the recipient died without reciprocating?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a gifted item given in expectation of recompense. If the recipient dies without reciprocating and the original item is found intact, there is no harm in the giver taking it back.
